correctness.rationale: For all kappa,sigma>0, 0<zc<H, and 0<rho<1, exact differentiation reduces stationary points to g(x)=(a-x)exp(-x^2/2), with unique negative maximum at x=-u. This proves the two-root classification and exact threshold rho_frag from whether the right stationary root lies below the surface. The strict derivative pattern +,-,+ yields necessary and sufficient existence of two positive-length superlevel depth bands and the exact allowable cutoff interval. A Taylor expansion of log g at -u gives the stated square-root extremum splitting and integration of Phi prime gives the exact 3/2 coefficient. All claims and boundary cases are proved in RESULT.md. value.rationale: The model deliberately isolates a motivated environmental tension: recovery of oxygen below a midwater minimum versus diminishing metabolic demand in cooler deep water. The exact threshold distinguishes continuous potential aerobic habitat from two separate viable depth bands, including a nontrivial surface-centre correction when the oxygen deficit lies shallow. It also locates the physiological bottleneck strictly above the oxygen-minimum centre and quantifies the onset window, resolving a meaningful physical-model question rather than an arbitrary numeric slice. No new physiological law, ecological barrier, or field predictive performance is claimed.
